rationale:
Evidence: iteration 2 (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.6, widened 5-sensor span at y 0.06, 16 mm footprints) scored 132.0, the best so far. It is the only design with a finish (oval, 1.88 s) and the highest progress on all three tracks (oval 0.45, s-bend 0.27, slalom 0.16). Both later single-field changes from it scored lower. Iteration 3 (ki 0.3 to 0.6) fell to 122.2, with the oval dropping from 218 to 192 and oscillation rising from 0.267 to 0.285. The round-1 critique also shows that the iteration-4 draft changes kp, kd and base_speed together, so its result could not be attributed to any one change.

What I accepted from the critique: (1) The kd increase to 1.0 has no support. Iteration 1 (kd 0.6) had lower oscillation than iteration 2 (kd 0.4), and iteration 3 showed that changing gains did not reduce oscillation, so I do not raise kd. (2) The score uses progress, line loss and rms, not oscillation, so oscillation targets are not my goal. (3) Oval finish time is 1.88 s, so speed is not the binding constraint on the oval. (4) The draft's changes are confounded, so I do not make any changes this round.

What I rejected: (a) Dropping base_speed to 1.3. Lower speed gives a time-limit risk for completion (500 points plus 60 time points), and iteration 0 at 1.8 gave more oval progress than iteration 1 at 1.5. (b) Dropping ki to 0. Removing the integral action that was present in the best run is not supported by any test. (c) Lowering kp to 2.8. Kp 3.0 produced the only finish and the highest progress, so I keep it.

What I kept: the iteration-2 geometry exactly, and the iteration-2 controller exactly (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.6, last_direction). This resubmission is the best-evidenced candidate. Expected result: the same distribution as iteration 2, with oval progress about 0.45 and the one-in-twenty finish chance. Decision rule for the next round: if max_error still sits at 0.06 with flat rms, and the s-bend and slalom still show line loss (0.65 and 0.8), the next single-variable test is a sensor-footprint or span change on those tracks, not a gain change. If progress stays flat, test base_speed 1.8 on its own, since the oval finish suggests time margin exists.
